content: Mesalamine is a medication used to treat ulcerative colitis, a specific bowel disease. It works by reducing symptoms such as diarrhea, rectal bleeding, and abdominal pain. This drug belongs to a class of medications called aminosalicylates. To use this medication, take it orally as directed by your doctor, typically three times daily. It can be taken with or without food, but some brands may require it to be taken on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after a meal. Swallow the medication whole without crushing, chewing, or breaking it. It is important to drink plenty of fluids during treatment unless otherwise instructed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also based on weight. Note that different brands of mesalamine may deliver varying amounts of the active medication, so follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. Regular use of this medication is necessary to achieve the best results. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, constipation, headache, or joint and muscle pain. Occasionally, you may notice whole or partial tablets in your stool; if this happens frequently, inform your doctor. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor believes the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, mesalamine may worsen ulcerative colitis or cause a severe allergic reaction. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking mesalamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminosalicylates (e.g., balsalazide, olsalazine), salicylates (e.g., aspirin, salsalate), sulfasalazine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Mesalamine may increase your sensitivity to sunlight, especially if you have skin conditions like eczema or atopic dermatitis. This medication is similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 should not take aspirin or aspirin-related medications (e.g., salicylates) if they have chickenpox, flu, an undiagnosed illness, or have recently received a vaccine, as this may increase the risk of serious complications. During pregnancy, mesalamine should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Mesalamine is very similar to balsalazide, olsalazine, and sulfasalazine, so avoid using these medications together unless directed by your doctor. Additionally, mesalamine may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine normetanephrine levels, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver and kidney function tests, may be performed before and during treatment to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. If the medication bottle contains a desiccant, keep it in the bottle and tightly close the lid when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
